occurrences.rawText: Introduction 1 Trust Funds1 are financial and administrative arrangements made between Development Partners (DPs) and one or more World Bank Group entities to meet diverse development needs including project preparation, technical assistance, advisory services, debt relief, post conflict transition, disaster recovery, climate change, and co-financing of lending projects. Trust funds contribute to the Bank Group’s mission of poverty reduction on a livable planet by supporting the design and implementation of development projects.

occurrences.rawText: This report provides aggregate financial information on trust fund operations administered individually or jointly by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Association (IDA), the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA). These four entities are collectively referred to as the “Bank Group.” This report is unaudited, and is not intended to represent the combined financial position of trust funds and programs administered by the Bank Group. Numbers presented for previous periods have been regrouped to conform to the current period presentation.

occurrences.nextContext: During FY24, a new FIF, Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF) was established. The Trust Fund has been established following the decision of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (“CBD”) at its Fifteen

occurrences.rawText: During FY24, a new FIF, Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF) was established. The Trust Fund has been established following the decision of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (“CBD”) at its Fifteenth Session (“COP 15”) to invite GEF to operate the Trust Fund. GBFF aims to support the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Five donors have contributed to-date to this FIF of which, majority of the funding was received from Canada ($55m) and Germany ($44m). TF reforms continued in FY24 with an aim to reduce fragmentation, increase strategic alignment and improve efficiencies of the trust fund portfolio by using fewer and larger Umbrella 2.0 Programs. As of June 30, 2024, 70 Umbrella programs (140 active trust funds) have been established. Four new umbrella programs - EGPS03, DIF, M - GROW and HSTRF have been initiated and activated in FY24.

occurrences.rawText: Commitment authority represents an upper limit up to which task teams can commit future disbursements at the individual TF level. The classes of assets that a trust fund could commit upon form the trust fund’s Basis of Commitment (BoC). The asset classes that can be committed against are either (i) cash, (ii) cash plus promissory notes, or (iii) cash plus promissory notes and contributions receivable. The default BoC for a trust fund is cash, but may be modified to include promissory notes receivable and/or contributions receivable with the approval of Director(s) in the unit managing the trust fund. occurrences.nextContext: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the B

occurrences.rawText: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the Bank Group entities. The Pool also includes funds held in ICSID's escrow accounts. IBRD maintains all assets underlying the trust funds’ fund balances separate and apart from the assets of the World Bank Group. IBRD, on behalf of the World Bank Group, invests the funds in liquid financial instruments such as government and agency obligations, time deposits, money-market securities and asset-backed securities, as well as swaps and a range of other derivative instruments. Additionally, the pool may also include equity securities. The investment composition within the pool is based on the investment horizons and cash flow profiles of the trust fund programs. Net investment income earned by the Pool is allocated to each trust fund based on its share of cash and investments in the Pool.
